paper: Yang, Kim, Jeong, Kim, Han, Lee — Intertwining orbital current order and superconductivity in Kagome metal, arXiv:2203.07365v2 (SciPost Physics, 2022)

open_questions.question: Does the full 2x2-folded (12-band-per-spin) chiral flux band structure reproduce the same total Chern numbers and edge-mode counts as the single-M closed-form kernel used here?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper's Table 1 and Fig. 3 edge spectra are computed in the extended 2x2 unit cell; the single-cell kernel confirms |C|=1 and the TRS-breaking gap but cannot directly render the folded bands or the zero-energy edge modes that physically manifest the Chern number.
open_questions.next_step: Build the 3Q-iCDW Hamiltonian in a real-space 2x2x(open-y) kagome supercell with per-bond Peierls phases matching Fig. 2, diagonalize, and count chiral edge modes per spin for all 4 cases.

open_questions.question: Do the LG quartic coefficients u1 ~= (0.003/tT^2) log(t Lambda^2/T) and u2 ~= 0.006/(tT^2) with u1 >> u2 actually select the 3Q-iCDW over 1Q/2Q as claimed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper's assertion that 3Q order minimizes the free energy rests on the sign and hierarchy of u1, u2 from integrating out the patch fermions; this is the quantitative backbone of the whole classification but was not recomputed here.
open_questions.next_step: Evaluate the one-loop particle-hole bubbles at the three vHS patches numerically, extract u1(T), u2(T), and verify u1 > u2 > 0 across the low-T regime T << t Lambda^2.

open_questions.question: How does each of the 4 iCDW patterns select its partner superconducting order parameter through the u4 CDW&SC coupling (Fig. 4)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper's headline application is inferring the SC order from the identified orbital-current order (and vice versa); the topological classification is only half the story.
open_questions.next_step: Derive the bilinear iCDW-SC coupling term in the LG functional and enumerate which singlet SC channel (s, d+-id, etc.) is favored for each of cases (i)-(iv).

open_questions.question: Is the sign of C_down at the balanced (2-of-3, e.g. (-i,i,i)) configuration robustly resolvable by a gauge-fixed numerical Chern calculation rather than by symmetry alone?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Our direct FHS index was ambiguous at the gapless balanced staggered config, forcing reliance on Eq. (4); an independent numerical sign would upgrade the agreement from symmetry-derived to fully numerical.
open_questions.next_step: Add a small symmetry-allowed gap-opening perturbation (or use the extended cell) so the balanced configs are gapped, then compute the FHS Chern sign directly and compare to the symmetry prediction.

open_questions.question: How stable is the classification against deviations from equal iCDW amplitudes |Phi_1|=|Phi_2|=|Phi_3| and from mu=0?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Real AV3Sb5 need not sit exactly at the vHS filling or have perfectly equal 3Q amplitudes; the topological labels could change if bands cross the Fermi level.
open_questions.next_step: Sweep unequal amplitudes and mu in the tight-binding model, tracking gap closings and Chern-number jumps to map the stability region of each pattern.

next_steps: Implement the extended 2x2 open-boundary supercell to render edge spectra (Fig. 3) and cross-check Chern via edge-mode counting.
Recompute LG coefficients u1, u2 from patch bubbles to verify 3Q selection.
Derive and tabulate the iCDW-to-SC pairing map from the u4 coupling term.
Gauge-fix or gap the balanced configs to obtain fully numerical C_down signs.
Perform amplitude/mu robustness sweeps for the topological phase boundaries.
